delivery.note: 24 papers: four in the narrator's hands from the start (the Board's letter he brought, the Collector's statement taken on arriving, and two printed tables), twenty earned by solving the 24 questions besides the goal, so four questions give nothing. truth: Saltmere, a small harbour town. The Custom House stands on the quay: the bond store in a stone vault below, the Long Room above. Henry Ashby, a Surveyor of the Board of Customs, is the narrator; he arrives on Wednesday 15 October at noon.

Jonas Prout, the Collector's clerk, has three times let brandy of Mr. Garrick's out of the bond store with no duty paid: 12 casks on 3 September, 12 on 24 September, 16 on 8 October. Each night Marsh, Garrick's carter, took them out through the quay gate on a pass initialled J.P. to Garrick's cellar in Mill Lane. After 1 October Prout wrote all three into the bond ledger as shipped for export in the brig Marigold.

Monday 13 October: the Board's letter reaches the Collector, Josiah Pell: the Surveyor comes on Thursday to compare every export entry with the vessels' papers. Pell tells Prout and nobody else. Prout tells Garrick, who stops the carting.

Tuesday 14 October. 5.30 pm Prout leaves. 6 pm the harbour-master, Odell, tells Prout (and nobody else) that the pier-head lamp wants oil and the watch should fill it at first light. 6 pm Pell puts the bond ledger in his bag, telling nobody, leaves his caped cloak on its peg, locks the street door and drives home to Cliff House, a mile and a half off. 7.40 pm Garrick takes the train to Tormouth. 9.30 pm high water; 9.45 pm the Marigold sails for Porthcarn; the bar is shut from 11.30 pm until 7.55 am.

10 pm Prout sits down to cribbage at the Anchor. At ten, eleven and twelve the night watch, Silas Crouch, tries the Custom House door, finds it fast and signs his book. 12.30 am Dr. Hume reaches Cliff House and sits with Pell, who cannot stand for gout, until 2.15.

12.45 am a man speaking low from the dark of the Anchor's yard door (Prout) gives the potboy twopence to tell Crouch that Mr. Odell wants him at the pier-head lamp directly. Crouch goes; the mole is a quarter of an hour's walk. He makes no round at one. Sam Tully, fishing at the mole head, sees him wait there.

1.15 am Prout pays and leaves the Anchor. He lets himself in with his key, takes the oil from the lamp room, heaps the books of the ledger press and fires them, not knowing the ledger is gone. He leaves in the Collector's cloak some minutes before the bell; the baker sees him and takes him for the Collector. He pushes the cloak under a boat on the hard.

1.45 am Crouch, back from the mole, sees the flames and rings the fire bell. The harbour-master logs it at 1.45 by the office clock; Mrs. Rowe hears it as the church clock, half an hour slow, strikes a quarter past one. Crouch says afterwards that he made every round; Prout that he was at the Anchor when the bell rang.

frame.says: The Long Room stove was cold, raked out and shut; no fire had been lit in it on Tuesday.
An empty lamp-oil can painted C.H. lay by the ledger press; in the lamp room below, the oil cupboard stood open with its key in the lock, and the can's place on the shelf was empty.
The ledger press stood open, its books pulled out into one heap before it, and the floor was burned deepest there.
The iron chest was locked and unbroken, and the week's duty money was in it.
The bond store below was unburnt, its door locked and its seal whole.
The lower half of the street door stands: the bolt of its lock is drawn back, and neither door nor frame is marked.
The windows on the quay are barred and the bars are whole.
By the Board's rule there are two keys to the street door, the Collector's and the clerk's; each showed the narrator his own on Wednesday.
On Thursday at noon the harbour office clock and the Anchor's clock agreed with the narrator's watch, set by railway time; the church clock stood half an hour behind it.
The narrator sat with Mr. Pell before the Board in London from 1 to 5 September.
On Thursday the narrator found a caped boat-cloak pushed under an upturned boat on the hard, reeking of lamp oil, its hem singed, the name J. Pell sewn inside the collar.
The pier-head lamp is at the end of the mole, a quarter of an hour's walk from the watch-box.
The bond ledger was put into the narrator's hands at Cliff House on Wednesday, unburnt.
The berths lie inside the quay gate; Mill Lane is in the town, outside it.

clues.source: The Board, to the Collector, in confidence; dated Friday 10 October, delivered on Monday the 13th
clues.says: The Surveyor will attend on Thursday the 16th to examine the bond ledger and compare every export entry with the vessels' papers.
He locked the street door at six on Tuesday, and his key was on his watch-chain all night.
The evening being mild, he left his caped cloak on its peg in the lobby.
He opened the Board's letter on Monday and told nobody of it but Mr. Prout.
On Tuesday, after Mr. Prout had gone at half past five, he put the bond ledger in his bag to cast the brandy account at home, and told nobody.
He reached Cliff House at half past twelve, found Mr. Pell unable to put his foot to the ground, and sat with him until a quarter past two.
Her master came home at half past six on Tuesday without his cloak.
He sat up over a great book until the pain took him; she sent for the doctor at midnight.
The watch is to try the Custom House door and sign the book every hour, from ten until six.
Signed at ten, eleven, twelve, two ("Custom House afire"), three, four, five and six.
At twelve: "C.H. door tried, fast."
He made every round and found the door fast each time.
He saw the flames in the Long Room windows from the quay and rang the fire bell.

clues.source: Peter Lobb, potboy at the Anchor
clues.says: As the taproom clock struck a quarter to one a man spoke low from the dark of the yard door and gave him twopence to run to the watch-box: Mr. Odell wants Crouch at the pier-head lamp directly, it wants oil. He never saw the man's face.
He told Crouch, who took his lantern and went off down the mole.
When the bell rang there were only his master, old Tully and himself in the house; Mr. Prout's chair was empty.

clues.source: Mr. Odell, the harbour-master, of himself
clues.says: At six on Tuesday he told Mr. Prout, and nobody else, that the pier-head lamp wanted oil and Crouch should fill it at first light; he sent no boy that night.

clues.source: The harbour log, in Mr. Odell's hand
clues.says: High water 9.30 p.m. Brig Marigold, Venn master, sailed 9.45 p.m. for Porthcarn with slate.
Fire bell rung on the quay at 1.45 a.m. by the office clock.
The fire bell began just as the church clock struck the quarter after one.

clues.source: Mr. Bales, landlord of the Anchor
clues.says: Mr. Prout sat at cribbage from ten, and paid and left at a quarter past one by the taproom clock.
When the bell rang Mr. Prout was not in the house.
He was at the Anchor from ten, was still at the table when the fire bell rang, and ran out with the rest.
His key of the street door has never been out of his pocket.

clues.source: Tobias Hearn, baker, at his oven door in Quay Street
clues.says: Some minutes before the bell a man in a caped cloak came out of the Custom House door, pulled it to and went off toward the hard.
It was the Collector: he knew him by the cloak; he did not see his face.

clues.source: Sam Tully, at his lines on the mole head from midnight
clues.says: Crouch came out along the mole soon after one, looked to the lamp and stood waiting; Tully watched his lantern all the way back, and it had just reached the quay when the bell began.
The bar carries water for vessels and boats only from two hours before high water until two hours after.
24 September: high water 4.40 a.m. and 5.05 p.m.; low water 10.50 a.m.
14 October: high water 9.30 p.m. 15 October: low water 3.40 a.m., high water 9.55 a.m.

clues.source: The Marigold's log, in Captain Venn's hand
clues.says: 1 to 6 September: at Cardiff, loading coal.

clues.source: The Marigold's log, in Captain Venn's hand
clues.says: 14 October: crossed Saltmere bar 10 p.m.; entries at midnight and at four; 15 October, 6 a.m., came to anchor at Porthcarn.

clues.source: The bond ledger, Garrick's brandy account
clues.says: 3 September: 12 casks delivered for export, per brig Marigold, Venn master, lying at the New Quay berth.
24 September: 12 casks for export per Marigold; cleared outwards and sailed at noon.
8 October: 16 casks for export per Marigold.

clues.source: A printed notice of the harbour commissioners
clues.says: The New Quay berth will be opened to vessels on 1 October.

clues.source: Three slips in one hand, each headed "Custom House, Saltmere" with its date
clues.says: 3 September, 24 September, 8 October: pass Marsh's cart with 12 (12, 16) casks from the bond store. J.P.
On 3 September, 24 September and 8 October, at eleven at night: Marsh's cart, casks, on a pass; out by the town gate, up Mill Lane.

clues.source: A note in Mr. Garrick's hand, dated Monday 13 October, given up by Marsh's wife
clues.says: Marsh: no more casks to my cellar in Mill Lane till I send word. The Board's man comes Thursday. L.G.
Saltmere 7.40 p.m. to Tormouth 9.10; the last train back leaves Tormouth 9.30 and reaches Saltmere 11.00; the first in the morning leaves 6.35 and arrives 8.05. Tormouth is fifty-eight miles by road.

clues.source: Mr. Keel, the station-master, who takes the tickets himself
clues.says: Mr. Garrick left by the 7.40 on Tuesday; nobody got down from the 11.00 but the curate; Mr. Garrick got down from the 8.05 on Wednesday.

rules_out.An accident of the stove: fr.stove: cold, raked out and shut; fr.oilcan and fr.press: oil brought up and books heaped to burn

rules_out.Yes, every one: c.watch_rule with c.watch_entries: no entry at one (the reader's own entry); c.crouch_rounds says otherwise and is set aside, linked as evidence

questions.answer: On the mole, at the pier-head lamp

rules_out.At the Anchor: c.on_mole: in Tully's sight on the mole from soon after one until the bell
rules_out.In the Custom House: c.on_mole, with fr.mole: a quarter of an hour away

questions.mechanic: one event at two times: two honest witnesses, two clocks
questions.asks: When was the fire bell first rung?

rules_out.At a quarter past one: fr.clocks: the church clock is half an hour slow, the office clock right; Mrs. Rowe's time is set aside (honest, and wrong as stated), linked as evidence

questions.asks: Was Mr. Prout at the Anchor when the bell rang?

rules_out.Yes: c.not_at_bell and c.chair_empty: two who were in the house say he was gone; c.prout_claim is set aside, linked as evidence

questions.mechanic: an alibi
questions.asks: Could Mr. Pell have been on the quay between half past twelve and two?

rules_out.Yes: c.doctor: at Cliff House in the doctor's sight from half past twelve until a quarter past two, and unable to stand

questions.mechanic: an alibi by the order of events: gone before, and no way back
questions.asks: Could Captain Venn have been ashore at Saltmere when the Custom House was fired?

rules_out.Yes: c.sailed: the brig left at 9.45; c.bar_rule with c.tide_oct14: nothing could cross the bar from 11.30 until 7.55; c.log_night: the master's hand in the log through the night, and Porthcarn at six

questions.mechanic: an alibi by the order of events: gone before, and no way back
questions.asks: Could Mr. Garrick have been at Saltmere when the Custom House was fired?

rules_out.Yes: c.garrick_trains: he left by the 7.40, was not on the last train back, and came by the 8.05; c.trains: no other train, and fifty-eight miles by road each way

questions.mechanic: two documents against each other
questions.asks: Was the Marigold at Saltmere on 3 September?

rules_out.Yes: c.cardiff: at Cardiff loading coal from 1 to 6 September

questions.mechanic: a document against a fixed time (the tide)
questions.asks: Could the Marigold have sailed at noon on 24 September?

rules_out.Yes: c.tide_sep24 with c.bar_rule: low water at 10.50, the bar shut from 6.40 a.m. until 3.05 p.m.

questions.mechanic: a document's own properties: it speaks of what did not yet exist at its date
questions.asks: Was the entry of 3 September written on that day?

rules_out.Yes: c.entry_sep3 names the New Quay berth; c.new_quay: there was no such berth before 1 October

rules_out.Josiah Pell's: c.passes: the first was written at the Custom House, Saltmere, on 3 September, and all three are in one hand; fr.london: Mr. Pell was in London, in the narrator's sight, from the 1st to the 5th

questions.answer: To Mr. Garrick's cellar in Mill Lane

rules_out.To the Marigold's berth: c.cart_out: out by the town gate; fr.mill_lane: the berths are inside it. c.note names the cellar in Mill Lane as Garrick's

questions.asks: Where was the Collector's cloak on Tuesday night?
questions.answer: On its peg in the Custom House

rules_out.At Cliff House with him: c.no_cloak: he came home without it (his housekeeper); c.pell_cloak: he says he left it on the peg

questions.mechanic: who could have known: an act that needs its doer to know a thing told to one person

rules_out.Josiah Pell: c.message: the sender knew the pier-head lamp wanted oil; c.errand: Mr. Odell told that to Mr. Prout and nobody else

rules_out.Silas Crouch: c.on_mole: on the mole until the bell; fr.keys with q.door: whoever came out had let himself in with a key, and the watch has none

questions.answer: To destroy the bond ledger before the Surveyor read it
others: To hide a theft of the duty money

rules_out.Out of spite against the Collector: q.aim: only the press was fired; q.entries with c.audit: the ledger held three false entries, and the Surveyor was to compare them with the vessels' papers two days later

questions.mechanic: means (an act that needs a key and its doer at the place), with every alibi
questions.asks: Who set fire to the Custom House?

rules_out.Josiah Pell: q.pell (c.doctor): at Cliff House and unable to stand; q.knew: he had the ledger himself and would not have fired the press for it; q.inside: the false entries were not his to hide
rules_out.Silas Crouch: fr.keys with q.door: he has no key; q.crouch (c.on_mole): on the mole
rules_out.Lucas Garrick: q.garrick (c.garrick_trains): at Tormouth; fr.keys: no key
rules_out.Captain Venn: q.venn (c.log_night): at sea; fr.keys: no key; q.entries: his brig carried none of it

points_to.Jonas Prout: fr.keys with c.prout_key: the other key, never out of his pocket; q.inside and q.why: the entries were his to hide; q.sender: he cleared the quay; q.gap: half an hour unaccounted for; q.figure: seen leaving
